diff: diff.patch (392 lines, 4 files, single wave, no chunking)

findings.title: Headline acceptance criterion unmet in Chrome: guarantor name/email still do not autofill (PR's own verification table), contradicting the shipped spec's AC and the original briefing acceptance
findings.evidence: Spec AC: "Given the apply form with a seeded vacancy, when the guarantor section is opened (required cohort or `has_guarantor` tick) and an autofill suggestion is clicked in a real Chromium, then `guarantor_name` / `guarantor_phone` / `guarantor_email` populate." PR body table: "Guarantor name / email | not filled | still suppressed by Chrome's 9-per-type cap (10th NAME_FULL / 11th EMAIL instance in the form — Chromium limit, not a form defect)".
findings.detail: The user-reported bug named the name/phone/email trio. After this PR, in Chrome, guarantor phone + employer autofill but name and email remain suppressed (10th NAME_FULL / 11th EMAIL instance past Chromium's kTypeValueFormFillingLimit=9; cap counting keyed per FieldType in form_filler.cc GetFillingSkipReasonsForField with no trigger-field exemption). The spec's Design Notes acknowledge the cap while its Acceptance Criteria section claims all three fields populate — the spec contradicts itself, and the original briefing's acceptance ("Chromium autofill popup populates the fields on click") is only partially met. The code change is correct and complete at the attribute layer; the gap is between the stated acceptance contract and the delivered outcome.
findings.recommended_fix: Renegotiate the acceptance contract explicitly: carve the Chrome-capped guarantor name/email fields out of spec AC #1 and the manual-check section (with the cap rationale), state the residual limitation in the PR title/description, and get explicit human sign-off on the partial fix — or scope the co-applicant-card de-duplication (the real lever) as a follow-up.

findings.title: Spec task list's exact-table/suffix-rule partition doesn't match the implemented partition (employer_ref_name, _amount)
findings.evidence: Spec: "exact-name table (existing 8 + job_title, employer_name, guarantor_employer, monthly_income_cents, guarantor_monthly_income_cents, employer_ref_name, amount) then suffix rules (_name, _email, _phone, _employer, _monthly_income_cents, _amount)". Code exact case: no employer_ref_name arm; code suffix rules: "_monthly_income_cents, _employer, _phone, _email, _name" — no _amount rule.
findings.detail: employer_ref_name resolves via the _name suffix (→ "name") and amount via the exact table (→ "transaction-amount") — outputs identical to the spec's golden mapping, only the internal partition differs. Harmless structurally, but the shipped spec artifact describes an implementation that doesn't match the code.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the spec task list to match the implemented partition (or add the two rules as defensive entries).

findings.title: tel-national pinned only at pure-function level — no co-applicant section-render assertion
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'tel-national' server/test/ matches only form_fields_test.gleam; the sole rendered-HTML autocomplete pin is guarantor_section_test.gleam:117-130 which never asserts tel-national. Co-applicant names are string-built in situation.gleam (prefix <> "[guarantor_phone]").
findings.detail: P3 defense-in-depth: mapping logic and the generic view_text_field render path are both pinned, so a regression in autocomplete_for would be caught. The unpinned surface is name-construction drift in situation.gleam or the co-applicant block ceasing to call view_text_field.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a render-level pin: render the co-applicant block with co_applicant_count>=1 and assert autocomplete="tel-national" in serialized HTML, mirroring guarantor_section_test's autocomplete_attributes_render_test.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.detail: P0 100%: full mapping pinned (exact table, suffix rules, off fallback, bracket normalization, tel-national). P1 90-95%: tel/tel-national boundary across all card indices, NAME_VS_ORG priority, conditional show/hide unregressed via pre-existing guarantor_section_test suite + the diff's render pin. Overall 90%+. Unit-level coverage is appropriate: pure SSR attribute on an existing renderer, no endpoint/DB/state change.
findings.recommended_fix: Gate is PASS; nothing blocks merge. Optional hardening: the co-applicant tel-national render pin above.

rejected.title: autocomplete_for has no honeypot guard; greedy suffix/exact matching can tokenize it
rejected.reason: False positive. The honeypot (_website) is rendered exclusively by view_honeypot_field (form_view.gleam:614-623) with its own hardcoded autocomplete="off" and never routes through autocomplete_for; autocomplete_for("_website") would return "off" anyway (no exact/suffix match). The spec's 'Never: no autofill tokens on the honeypot' constraint is satisfied. The finding describes a hypothetical future rename, not a present defect.

reviewer_agreement: No finding was reported by two or more lenses. The blocker (AC-1) was reported by the acceptance lens and independently confirmed by the orchestrator's verification pass.
verdict_reason: 1 blocker: the shipped spec's headline acceptance criterion (guarantor_name/guarantor_email populate in Chrome) is contradicted by the PR's own real-browser verification table; the spec artifact is internally contradictory (AC vs Design Notes). Code itself is correct, complete at the attribute layer, and well-tested.
